name: Dominica
summary: No free movement for anyone. Dominica has the cheapest Caribbean citizenship route: USD 200,000 donation for a single applicant (Economic Diversification Fund) or USD 200,000 in approved real estate plus a USD 75,000 government fee. The Work in Nature extended stay visa is for remote workers. UK visa-free access ended in July 2023 and the US restricts entry at some level since December 2025.
naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation residence period not verified in this research; see open questions.
dual_citizenship_note: Dual citizenship is allowed for CBI citizens (not verified against the Citizenship Act this pass).

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: Economic Diversification Fund (EDF)
routes.summary: A USD 200,000 non-refundable contribution for a single applicant (USD 250,000 for a family of up to four) gives citizenship.
routes.requirements: USD 200,000 single applicant; USD 250,000 main applicant plus up to 3 dependants; USD 25,000 per extra dependant under 18; USD 40,000 per extra dependant 18+. Fees: processing USD 1,000; due diligence USD 7,500 main, USD 4,000 per dependant 16+; naturalisation certificate USD 500; interview USD 1,000 (mandatory for 16+). Applications only through authorised agents (CBI Regulations 2024). Banned: Belarus, Russia, northern Iraq (Kurdistan region); Yemen suspended (circular 15 January 2024); North Korea, Sudan and Iran refused unless applicant has not lived there for 10 years, holds no substantial assets and has not done business there.
routes.investment_options: EDF USD 200,000 (single); approved real estate from USD 200,000 (held 3 years; 5 if resold to another CBI applicant).
routes.fees_note: Processing 1,000 + due diligence 7,500 + certificate 500 + interview 1,000. Enhanced due diligence may cost more.
routes.physical_presence: None stated on the CBIU pages; see open questions.
routes.family: Spouse, children, parents and grandparents who rely on the main applicant count as dependants.
routes.tax_note: Citizenship alone does not end tax residence elsewhere.

sources.title: UK strips Saint Lucia of visa-free access (notes Dominica lost it July 2023)

routes.name: Citizenship by Investment: Approved real estate
routes.summary: USD 200,000 in an approved project, held 3 years, plus a USD 75,000 government fee for a single applicant.
routes.requirements: Minimum USD 200,000 in an approved project. Hold 3 years from the grant of citizenship (5 years if resold to another CBI applicant). Government fee USD 75,000 main applicant, USD 100,000 with up to 3 dependants; USD 25,000 per extra dependant under 18, USD 40,000 per extra dependant 18+. Plus processing 1,000, due diligence 7,500, certificate 500, interview 1,000. Banned: Belarus, Russia, northern Iraq (Kurdistan region); Yemen suspended (circular 15 January 2024); North Korea, Sudan and Iran refused unless applicant has not lived there for 10 years, holds no substantial assets and has not done business there.
routes.physical_presence: None stated on the CBIU pages.

routes.name: Work in Nature (WIN) extended stay visa
routes.summary: An extended stay of up to 18 months for remote workers earning from outside Dominica.
routes.requirements: Reported by secondary guides: 18+, no criminal record, ability to work remotely for non-Dominican employer or own business, income about USD 50,000 a year or proof of means to support family, health insurance. Local employment prohibited. Reported not renewable. Official page not read.
routes.fees_note: Sources conflict: USD 100 application plus USD 800 individual or USD 1,200 family, or USD 900 total.
routes.tax_note: Reported exempt from local tax on foreign-source income; unverified.

open_questions: Residence/presence requirement after citizenship not stated on CBIU pages.
Official WIN extended stay fee and renewal rules not found.
Retiree/permanent residence routes for non-citizens not found.
Ordinary naturalisation residence period not found.
US restriction status for Dominica: one source says visa validity was cut from 10 years to 3 months in December 2025; Passport Legacy lists Antigua only.
CBIU pages show no 2025-2026 changes in amounts; the Regulations 2024 are the basis for fees.
ECCIRA start date: sources conflict (April 2026, Q2 2026, September 2026, 'late 2026', or not yet operational as of 8 August 2026). Check eccira.org.

Reported European Commission letter of 25 June 2026 asking the Eastern Caribbean states to end citizenship programmes by 1 June 2028 comes from one professional source (Passport Legacy); not checked against a Commission document.
